newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen Breaux offers IDB allocation bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen Breaux offers IDB allocation bill.

text.p: States would have more flexibility to use industrial development bond (IDB) money for important construction projects under legislation introduced on Thursday by U.S. Sen. John Breaux, D-La., Breaux's office said.

Currently, states can issue $50 per resident or $150 million, whichever is greater, in IDBs annually. But while they can carry forward unused volume cap allocations for up to three years, they must allocate any unused cap to specific uses at the end of each year.

Breaux said he wants to see states have more options in how they spend the $150 million a year when they have an unused cap. His bill would allow states to reallocate unused bond money to another type of project needed elsewhere in the state.
"Tax-exempt bonds are essential for states to finance industrial development projects, ranging from small manufacturing facilities to pollution control and resource recovery facilities," Breaux said.
"I want to help states fund industrial development and better allocate their scarce tax-exempt bond authority," he said.

The bill, which is co-sponsored by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, R-N.Y., also would increase from $10 million to $20 million the limit on capital expenditures that a company can maintain and still qualify for industrial bond money, Breaux's office said.
The increase would reflect the effects of inflation since 1978 when the program was first created and it correct for the effects of future inflation on a company's real worth, Breaux's office said.
